correctness.rationale: Matrix-unit commutators and invertibility of two imply each semisimple first factor has a free rank-one kernel of size q^k and trace-orthogonal image. A primitive linear equation on three ring coordinates gives q^(2k+j-2) lifts per allowed residual point. The residual quadratic-plane computation yields q(q-1), 0 or (q-1)(q-d)/2 points depending on isotropy/splitting; direct summation gives the zero fiber and exceptional target count. The entire formula and total pairs were verified by standalone explicit enumeration for six rings, including all 387420489 ordered pairs over each of two distinct length-three rings.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Stasinski proves qualitative (and in n=2 odd) commutator representations without choosing a split/nonsplit type; his existence does not imply all split factors suffice nor the exact anisotropic failure locus. Choosuwan et al give all-matrix determinant counts, not pair counts constrained by a bracket and residue type. There is no full coverage from these sources without nontrivial new orthogonal-plane reduction.

originality.rationale: The candidate counts split and nonsplit residue-square-class restricted first-factor witnesses for every prescribed trace-zero commutator over all odd-residue finite chain rings. Direct primary full-text inspections of qualitative commutator theorems, full determinant counts, and the closest public constrained square-zero and unrestricted Takiff counts found no implication of its sharp split/nonsplit support dichotomy. A stronger unidentified orbit-incidence theorem remains possible; priority is qualified, not certified.

value.rationale: Split/nonsplit first factors are the natural toral spectral types of rank-one Lie theory. Prescribing that type asks an algebraically meaningful commutator-witness existence question. The theorem gives complete finite-chain-ring labeled fibers, proves split type surjective for all targets, and isolates a sharp nonsplit obstruction of exactly (q^2-1)(q^(3k)-1)/(q^3-1) leading-isotropic targets; this reveals a persistent arithmetic dichotomy not captured by unrestricted commutator existence, and is uniform across unequal ring characteristics and all depths.
